A 'final' entry must also carry tool, model, prompt, references, generatedAt and licence, and may list optimised variants. assets.alt: The Tap Room: a long dark wooden bar with stools, bottles on the shelves, a small television glowing above it, and rain on the front window.
The Back Room: a small private snug with a round table, four chairs, one lamp, and a window onto a rainy alley.
The Kitchen: a clean counter and a steel sink under a single lamp, late at night.
The Back Stairs: a narrow, plain wooden staircase lit by one weak bulb.
The Upstairs Hall: a low corridor of doors with worn carpet and a rainy window at the far end.
Room 5: a slept-in bed, an open suitcase on a wooden chair, and a lit lamp on the side table beside a rainy window.
Ray Kowalski, the bartender: a broad-shouldered man in his forties with tired, kind eyes, a white shirt with rolled sleeves and a bar towel on his shoulder.
Dwight Wentworth, the local businessman: a lean, neatly groomed man in his fifties in a brown three-piece suit with a tie pin.
Carol Wentworth: a composed, watchful woman in her late thirties with dark shoulder-length hair, in a camel wool coat over a cream blouse.
Edna Marsh, the innkeeper: a practical woman in her sixties with pinned-up grey hair, a cardigan, glasses on a chain and keys at her belt.
Dennis Pruett, the retired mill foreman: a ruddy, friendly man in his fifties in a flannel shirt and a worn work jacket.
Gerald Fenn, the portrait painter: a man in his late fifties with paint-stained cuffs and a sardonic, observant expression.
A heavy glass ashtray, wiped smooth with no ash in it, beside a pale ring left on the dark wood.
One empty tumbler with a thin brown film in the bottom, standing beside a lamp.
A folded sheet of paper lying on old floorboards, as if it had been kicked there.
A wooden tabletop radio with a softly glowing amber dial on the dark counter of an inn bar at night, with rain on the window behind it.
